newsitem.title: CHINA: China urges Ukraine to be vigilant against Taiwan.
newsitem.headline: China urges Ukraine to be vigilant against Taiwan.

text.p: China hopes Ukraine will remain vigilant against Taiwan's "dollar diplomacy" overtures and its attempts to break out of diplomatic isolation, the official Xinhua news agency said in an overnight report.

The call came one day after South African President Nelson Mandela announced that Pretoria would switch diplomatic recognition to Beijing from Taipei in a blow to the wealthy but diplomatically isolated island.
As China savoured its latest victory in a five-decade-old diplomatic tug-of-war with Taiwan, it gave no indication it was about to let down its guard against the island.

"We hope that Ukraine can... maintain a high level of vigilance against the Taiwan authorities' 'dollar diplomacy'," Chinese Vice Foreign Minister Tian Zengpei told his visiting Ukrainian counterpart Konstantin Grishchenko on Thursday.
Beijing and Taipei have been diplomatic rivals since Chiang Kai-shek's Republic of China government fled into exile in Taiwan at the end of the Chinese civil war in 1949.
China has accused Taiwan of using its wealth to buy diplomatic allies. Beijing regards Taiwan as a rebel province ineligible for foreign ties.

"We hope that Ukraine can understand the sensitivity and importance of the Taiwan question, stick to the principle of 'one China'...so as not to allow the Taiwan issue to disturb the development of Sino-Ukrainian relations," Tian said.
In August, China cancelled a visit to Ukraine by a senior official in an apparent protest against a visit to the former Soviet republic by Taiwan's Vice-President Lien Chan.
